title: Exercise 1: Absorption spectrum of curcumin
body:
Curcumin is a yellow food colouring (E100) and the main pigment in turmeric (Curcuma longa). The file curcumine_EtOH.csv, available on Madoc, contains the spectrum of curcumin in ethanol.

Using pandas to create a DataFrame (organising data into columns)

Using pandas (usually imported with the alias pd) lets you organise datasets into structured tables called DataFrames. These DataFrames can be created from .csv files using:

df = pd.read_csv('chemin_du_fichier.csv', paramètres)

Important parameters for reading a CSV file: delimiter='...' specifies the value separator (useful when it is not a comma). For example: '\t' for a tab, ';' for a semicolon. usecols=[...] reads only the specified columns. skiprows=... specifies the number of lines to skip at the start of the file. Reading and handling DataFrame data:

print(df) : Affiche le tableau généré.
print(df.columns) : Affiche le nom des colonnes.
df['nom_de_la_colonne'] : Sélectionne une colonne entière (utile pour des analyses

This selects an entire column, which is useful for analysis or plotting. Example of plotting a graph with matplotlib:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(df['nom_de_la_colonne_x'], df['nom_de_la_colonne_y'])
plt.xlabel('Nom de la colonne X')
plt.ylabel('Nom de la colonne Y')
plt.title('Titre du graphique')
plt.show()

Instructions:

1. Display the data in curcumine_EtOH.csv (available on Madoc), along with the column names of the resulting DataFrame.

2. Plot absorbance as a function of wavelength.

Using special characters in Matplotlib.

Matplotlib can display special characters in graph legends and annotations, including Greek letters. To do this, enclose the special-character command between $ signs in a text string.

Command Character Command Character Command Character

\alpha α \eta η \pi π \beta β \theta θ \rho ρ \gamma γ \lambda λ \sigma σ \delta δ \mu μ \phi φ \epsilon ε \nu ν \chi χ \zeta ζ \xi ξ \omega ω

3. Find the wavelength corresponding to the maximum of the absorption spectrum and indicate it on the graph with a dotted line.

Using Pandas to find maxima and minima.

As with numpy and ndarrays, you can find extrema in DataFrames. The max and min methods are available for this, and idxmax() and idxmin() return the corresponding index labels.

title: Exercise 2: Calibration line and calculation of the molar absorption coefficient of curcumin
body:
The file curcumine_concentration.csv, available on Madoc, contains absorbance values at the absorption maximum of curcumin in ethanol at different concentrations.

Instructions:

1. Display the data in curcumine_concentration.csv (available on Madoc), along with the column names of the resulting DataFrame.

2. Plot absorbance as a function of concentration and remove any outliers.

Removing data from a DataFrame.

Data are removed from a DataFrame using:

df.drop(nom_de_la_ligne_ou_colonne, axis=0_ou_1) # 0 pour

Use 0 for a row or 1 for a column.

3. Perform a linear regression and display the slope and the coefficient of determination R2.

Using linregress to perform a linear regression.

The linregress function is available in the scipy.stats module. It performs a linear regression and returns an object with six attributes (its legacy unpacking behaviour provides five values): a: slope (slope). b: y-intercept (intercept). c: correlation coefficient (rvalue), where c² is the coefficient of determination (R²). d: p-value (pvalue). e: standard error of the slope (stderr). f: standard error of the intercept (intercept_stderr).

4. Knowing that the cuvette path length is 1 cm, deduce the molar absorption coefficient.

title: Exercise 3: Plotting the line spectra of hydrogen and helium
body:
The files H41.csv and He.csv, available on Madoc, contain the absorption-line data for hydrogen and helium, respectively.

1. Display the data in H41.csv and He.csv, along with the column names of the resulting DataFrames.

We now want to plot these two line spectra. To display several plots, use:

plt.subplot(xxx, paramètres_graphiques)

• The first digit specifies the number of rows in the grid of plots.

• The second digit specifies the number of columns.

• The third digit specifies the plot number within the layout. In the plotting parameters, facecolor='...' sets the plot background colour. You can also display the lines using a colour palette. Some palettes are designed to represent the different colours of the visible spectrum.

Of these four palettes, the ‘turbo’ colormap most closely resembles the visible spectrum. To use a colour palette, retrieve it with:

plt.get_cmap('nom_de_la_colormap')

A colormap associates its first colour with the lowest value in the range and its last colour with the highest value. To assign visible-spectrum colours to wavelengths, you therefore need to:

• Define the colormap range using the visible-spectrum limits (350 nm to 750 nm).

• Normalise each wavelength to a value between 0 and 1 according to its position within this range.

2. Plot the two line spectra one below the other over the visible range (350 to 750 nm), with a black background and each line assigned the corresponding visible-spectrum colour.
